claims.head: Who blinks first?
claims.body: The Avalanche are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Devils are one of the best at keeping shots away. We think the Avalanche still get theirs.

claims.head: Strength against strength
claims.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Avalanche are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.

claims.head: The Avalanche like Nelson’s line against Hughes’s
claims.call: The Avalanche’s L2 (Landeskog, Nelson and Kadri) spends at least 36% of its 5-on-5 time against the Devils’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Avalanche keep sending Nelson’s line (Landeskog, Nelson and Kadri) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jared Bednar keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Devils’ second line is Gritsyuk, Hughes and Bratt.
claims.nums: At home: 36% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against second lines, about 25% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Jared Bednar likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Devils’ second line.

COL.head: The Avalanche start a half-step ahead
COL.body: Even though New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents lately, the Devils are on the second night of a back-to-back, and Colorado has home-ice advantage. The Devils can still swing it if their penalty kill holds up.

NJD.head: Close, but the Avalanche have the slight edge
NJD.body: Even though New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents lately, the Devils are on the second night of a back-to-back, and Colorado has home-ice advantage. The Devils’ best way to tip it is a penalty kill that holds up.

story.head: The Devils come in hot
paras: The Devils won the first meeting this season, 4-3 in New Jersey. The Avalanche are 6-5-1. The Devils have won four straight, the last a 5-1 rout of Dallas.

It’s strength against strength: the Avalanche are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Devils are one of the best at keeping shots away. At home, Jared Bednar likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Devils’ second line.
